requirements.requirement: Build AI product experiences using language model APIs
Design structured generation pipelines for LLM outputs
Validate model output and handle non-conforming responses
Design retrieval grounded in source documents
Own frontend integration in TypeScript and React
Evaluate latency and cost of AI systems
Machine learning model training not required

overallAssessment.narrative: Reg is a direct fit for an AI application engineering role: he has shipped production LLM features end to end — tool calling, schema-constrained generation, output validation and failure handling, and runtime context design — as a TypeScript/Next.js application owner. He pairs that AI work with whole-system product ownership, secure API and authorization experience, and production systems serving real customers. Nothing in his background suggests a material mismatch for this role's scope.

themes.title: Production LLM feature engineering
themes.narrative: Reg built CModel's strategic assistant in TypeScript/Next.js with the Vercel AI SDK: tool calling, schema-constrained generation, and an explicit validate-then-accept/retry/repair/reject boundary between model output and application state. At Reaccord he extended this with model-independent architecture that separates provider configuration from prompts, output shape, validation, and UI — directly relevant to managing latency and cost as models change.

themes.title: Retrieval and context design
themes.narrative: Reg designs what models see rather than dumping everything into prompts. CModel's assistant combines provided organization/page context with selective tool-based retrieval; Reaccord assembles task-specific context from persistent user state so the application owns context selection. This is exactly the retrieval-grounded-in-source-documents capability the role targets.

themes.title: Backend, security, and frontend ownership in TypeScript
themes.narrative: Reg implements and maintains OAuth/API integrations across Microsoft 365 and other third-party systems, and has designed delegated authorization with role-scoped permissions in production. His data-modeling work pairs durable domain structures with Zod-validated contracts for AI-generated state. He ships full-stack in TypeScript, React, and Next.js.

themes.title: Production operations under real constraints
themes.narrative: Reg has operated live systems serving thousands of users and real transactions, where debugging crossed application, backend, and external-service boundaries. At MusicBreakr he made explicit tradeoffs between data freshness, scheduling, batch size, and operating cost — the same observability and cost-conscious reasoning AI systems demand.

themes.title: Product collaboration and 0-to-1 ownership
themes.narrative: Reg owns workflows from product definition through production, translating ambiguous founder-level requirements into shipped features. At CModel he also initiated an agentic team development process combining shared technical context, AI-assisted development, engineer review, and CI/CD controls — evidence he raises the whole team's output, not just his own.

interviewQuestions: Walk me through a case where model output repeatedly failed validation — how did you decide between retry, repair, and reject, and what did that boundary look like in code?
How did you measure and manage latency and cost in the strategic assistant or Reaccord's AI features as usage or model choices changed?
Tell me about a production AI feature where the context or retrieval design turned out to be wrong in practice — how did you detect it and what did you change?
